etmCategoryList.name: SECTORAL-AUTO & TRANSPORTATION
etmCategoryList.desc: Invest in companies across the auto and transportation value chain — including OEMs, EV makers, auto ancillaries, and logistics players — benefiting from rising mobility demand and the ongoing EV transition.

etmCategoryList.name: GOLD
etmCategoryList.desc: Invest in gold through funds that track gold prices — offering a convenient, cost-effective alternative to buying physical gold without storage or safety concerns.
etmCategoryList.goal: ["Acts as a hedge against inflation and currency depreciation, preserving purchasing power over time","Low correlation with equity markets, making it a strong portfolio diversifier during market downturns","No risk of theft or making charges — own gold digitally at lower cost than physical gold"]

etmCategoryList.name: SILVER
etmCategoryList.desc: Invest in silver through funds that track silver prices — offering a convenient, cost-effective alternative to buying physical silver without storage or safety concerns.
etmCategoryList.goal: ["Acts as a hedge against inflation and economic uncertainty, helping preserve purchasing power over time","Low correlation with equity markets, making it a useful portfolio diversifier during market volatility","No risk of theft or making charges — own silver digitally at lower cost than physical silver"]

etmCategoryList.name: EQUITY_LARGE_CAP
etmCategoryList.desc: Large-cap mutual funds are the type of equity funds that invest primarily in the stocks of largest 100 companies (highest market capitalization) of India. These companies are some of the biggest brands in our country, and most Indians use their products daily.

etmCategoryList.name: EQUITY_LARGE_AND_MIDCAP
etmCategoryList.desc: Large and mid-cap mutual funds are equity funds that invest in India's top 250 companies. These funds bring together India's biggest companies and mid-sized companies that are challenging those big companies for the top slot.

etmCategoryList.name: EQUITY_MULTI_CAP
etmCategoryList.desc: Multi cap funds invest in companies of all sizes and across sectors. Unlike large or mid cap funds, they can decide how money gets allocated between big, mid-sized, and small companies. This flexibility also allows them to make changes in the portfolio as market conditions change.

etmCategoryList.name: EQUITY_MID_CAP
etmCategoryList.desc: Mid-cap mutual funds are equity funds that invest in the stocks of mid-sized companies (as per market capitalisation) of India. The companies are some of the fastest-growing companies in India and are at a stage today's leaders were a few years back.

etmCategoryList.name: EQUITY_SMALL_CAP
etmCategoryList.desc: Small-cap funds are the type of equity funds that invest in small companies' stocks (with market capitalisation of less than Rs. 5,000 crores) in India. These companies are beyond the top 250 companies and are mostly unheard of in our daily lives. While they can deliver fantastic returns, small-cap companies are incredibly volatile, and you can see losses in short to medium-term

etmCategoryList.name: EQUITY_VALUE_ORIENTED
etmCategoryList.desc: Value equity funds follow the investing principles popularized by legends like Warren Buffet. These funds look for stocks that are currently trading on discount due to some reason but have long term potential.

etmCategoryList.name: EQUITY_ELSS
etmCategoryList.desc: ELSS (Equity Linked Savings Scheme) funds are equity mutual funds that offer tax deductions under Section 80C up to ₹1.5 lakh per year while helping investors build long-term wealth through investments in the stock market. With a 3-year lock-in period, they offer the dual benefit of tax savings and potential higher returns, which are ideal for investors investing around ₹9,000 per month.

etmCategoryList.name: EQUITY_SECTORAL_BANKING
etmCategoryList.desc: Banking sector funds are a type of equity mutuals fund that invest exclusively in banking and financial services companies. These funds are highly sensitive to interest rate changes, economic cycles, and regulatory policies affecting the banking industry. Since they focus on a single sector, they carry higher risk compared to diversified equity funds.

etmCategoryList.name: EQUITY_SECTORAL_INFRASTRUCTURE
etmCategoryList.desc: Infrastructure mutual funds are equity funds that invest only in companies related to infrastructure development. These funds focus on industries such as construction, power, transportation, and telecommunications.

etmCategoryList.name: EQUITY_SECTORAL_PHARMA
etmCategoryList.desc: Pharma sector mutual funds are type of equity funds that invest only in pharmaceutical and healthcare-related companies. These funds focus on businesses involved in drug manufacturing, biotechnology, hospitals, medical devices, and other healthcare services. Since they are concentrated in a single sector, pharma funds carry higher risk compared to diversified equity funds, as their performance depends on factors like regulatory policies, drug approvals, global healthcare trends, and market demand for medical products.

etmCategoryList.name: EQUITY_SECTORAL_TECHNOLOGY
etmCategoryList.desc: Technology mutual funds are type of equity funds that invest only in technology and IT-related companies. These funds focus on businesses involved in software development, IT services, semiconductors, artificial intelligence, cloud computing, and other emerging technologies. Since they are concentrated in a single sector, technology funds carry higher risk compared to diversified equity funds, as their performance depends on factors like innovation, market competition, global demand for tech services, and regulatory changes in the tech industry.

etmCategoryList.name: EQUITY_THEMATIC
etmCategoryList.desc: Thematic funds are equity mutual funds that invest in stocks tied to a theme. These funds are more broad-based then sectoral fund, as they pick companies and sectors united by an idea. For instance, an infrastructure theme fund will invest in cement, power, steel, among other sectors

etmCategoryList.name: EQUITY_THEMATIC_DIVIDEND_YIELD
etmCategoryList.desc: Dividend yield mutual funds are equity funds that invest in stocks of companies that declare dividends regularly.

etmCategoryList.name: EQUITY_THEMATIC_MNC
etmCategoryList.desc: MNC mutual funds are thematic equity mutual funds that invest primarily in stocks of multinational corporations (MNCs) listed in Indian stock exchanges.

etmCategoryList.name: EQUITY_THEMATIC_ENERGY
etmCategoryList.desc: Energy funds are thematic equity funds that invest in stocks of energy sector companies. These companies are generally involved in renewable energy, conventional energy (like coal, thermal power, oil & gas exploration, distribution, refining), energy infrastructure development, innovation, etc.

etmCategoryList.name: EQUITY_THEMATIC_PSU
etmCategoryList.desc: PSU thematic funds are equity mutual funds that mainly invest in stocks of publicly listed government-owned companies know as public sector units (PSUs).

etmCategoryList.name: EQUITY_THEMATIC_CONSUMPTION
etmCategoryList.desc: Consumption mutual funds are equity mutual funds that invest in stocks of companies which are benefiting from consumer-driven demand such as companies related to FMCG, retail, auto, automobiles, electronics, healthcare, etc.

etmCategoryList.name: EQUITY_INTERNATIONAL
etmCategoryList.desc: International funds are equity funds that invest in stocks of companies listed outside of India. These funds help you invest in some of the biggest companies in the world.

etmCategoryList.name: DEBT_LONG_DURATION
etmCategoryList.desc: Long Duration funds are debt funds that lend to quality companies for 5 or more years. The tenure of loan means that investment is more or less exposed to the entire economic cycle and hence is inherently more risky than other Debt Funds.

etmCategoryList.name: DEBT_MEDIUM_TO_LONG_DURATION
etmCategoryList.desc: These are debt funds that lend to corporates for a duration of 4-7 years. This long lending horizon means investments in all probability will a full economic cycle and therefore have a higher risk than short duration funds. This long lending horizon makes them extremely vulnerable to changes in interest rates due to the reversal of economic or business cycle.

etmCategoryList.name: DEBT_MEDIUM_DURATION
etmCategoryList.desc: Medium duration funds are debt funds that lend to quality companies for 3 or more years. The longer tenure of loan means these funds returns are subject to the interest rate changes that borrowing companies undergo due to positive or negative economic cycles over time.

etmCategoryList.name: DEBT_SHORT_DURATION
etmCategoryList.desc: Short term funds are debt funds that lend to companies for a period of 1 to 3 years. These funds mostly take exposure only in quality companies that have proven record of repaying their loans on time as well as have sufficient cash flows from their business operations to justify the borrowing.

etmCategoryList.name: DEBT_LOW_DURATION
etmCategoryList.desc: Low Duration Funds are debt funds that lend to companies for a period of 6 to 12 months. There relatively longer lending duration makes them a little more volatile than liquid or Ultra Short Duration Funds, but they don't have any Stock Market or Equity Instruments & hence are relatively safer funds to invest.

etmCategoryList.name: DEBT_ULTRA_SHORT_DURATION
etmCategoryList.desc: Ultra Short Duration Funds are debt funds that lend to companies for a period of 3 to 6 months. Although these are low-risk funds owing to their low lending duration, they are slightly above liquid funds in the risk spectrum but still one of the lowest risk categories of Schemes to invest in.

etmCategoryList.name: DEBT_LIQUID
etmCategoryList.desc: Liquid funds are debt funds that lend to companies for a period of up to 91 days. These are the safest funds amongst all the mutual fund categories, owing to their extremely low lending duration.

etmCategoryList.name: DEBT_MONEY_MARKET
etmCategoryList.desc: Money Market Funds are debt funds that lend to companies for a period of up to 1 year. These Funds are designed in a manner that allows the fund manager to generate higher returns while keeping risk under control through adjustment of lending duration. Higher loan tenure usually comes with higher returns.

etmCategoryList.name: DEBT_OVERNIGHT
etmCategoryList.desc: Overnight funds are debt funds that lend to corporates for 1 business day. The corporates eligible for borrowing through this route are regulated and are mostly banks, insurance companies, mutual funds, provident funds, and NBFCs

etmCategoryList.name: DEBT_DYNAMIC_BOND
etmCategoryList.desc: Dynamic bond funds are debt funds that 'dynamically' manage the lending duration. These funds are constructed in a way that allows fund managers to use interest rates movements in the economy as an opportunity to generate higher returns. This is done by increasing or reducing the lending duration depending on whether the interest rates are heading down or up

etmCategoryList.name: DEBT_CORPORATE_BOND
etmCategoryList.desc: Corporate bond funds are debt funds that lend at least 80% of their money to companies with the highest possible credit rating. This rating is given only to companies that are financially strong and have a high probability of paying lenders on time.

etmCategoryList.name: DEBT_CREDIT_RISK
etmCategoryList.desc: Credit risk funds are debt funds that lend at least 65% of their money to not-so-highly rated companies. The borrowers pay higher interest charges as a way to compensate for their lower credit rating, which translates into a higher risk for the lender due to an increased possibility of default. Although these funds lend mostly for short duration, they are still one of the riskiest in the category.

etmCategoryList.name: DEBT_BANKING_AND_PSU
etmCategoryList.desc: Banking and PSU funds are debt funds that lend only to banks and public sector companies. The high quality of borrowers allows these loans mean the risk of default is very less. However, they do get affected if interest rates in the economy go up.

etmCategoryList.name: DEBT_FLOATER
etmCategoryList.desc: Floater funds are debt funds that invest at least 65% of their money in floating-rate bonds. The interest these bonds pay change as the interest rates in the economy change. A periodic resetting of rates to keep them in sync with market rates.

etmCategoryList.name: DEBT_FMP
etmCategoryList.desc: FMP (Fixed Maturity Plan) is a debt-oriented mutual fund that invests in fixed-income securities whose maturities align with the fund’s tenure, aiming to offer predictable returns when held till maturity.

etmCategoryList.name: DEBT_GILT
etmCategoryList.desc: Gilt funds are debt funds that invest primarily in government securities. These funds have no risk of non-payment of interest or principal amount but get affected by interest rate movements as the Government borrowing typically happens to be for a longer duration.

etmCategoryList.name: DEBT_GILT_WITH_10_YEAR_CONSTANT_DURATION
etmCategoryList.desc: These are debt funds that invest money in government securities. The Fund Managers don't actively manage the lending duration & instead keeps it constant at 10 Years at an overall portfolio level. These funds don't buy or sell government securities just because interest rates are moving in the economy. These funds almost work like an Index Fund for 10 Year G-Sec.

etmCategoryList.name: HYBRID_AGGRESSIVE_HYBRID
etmCategoryList.desc: Aggressive Hybrid Funds are balanced funds invest primarily in stocks with some allocation to FD-like instruments. Spreading out of investments means these funds are less risky than pure equity funds with almost similar returns in the long run.

etmCategoryList.name: HYBRID_BALANCED_HYBRID
etmCategoryList.desc: Balanced hybrid funds invest an equal amount in stocks and FD-like instruments. These funds provide you a truly balanced portfolio that combines growth and stability.

etmCategoryList.name: HYBRID_CONSERVATIVE_HYBRID
etmCategoryList.desc: Conservative Hybrid funds invest primarily in fixed-income instruments with some allocation to stocks. These funds look to provide more returns than bank fixed deposits without taking too much risk.

etmCategoryList.name: HYBRID_EQUITY_SAVINGS
etmCategoryList.desc: Equity Saving Funds are hybrid mutual funds which invest almost an equal amount in stocks, fixed-income instruments, and arbitrage opportunities (risk-free hedging strategies). These funds tend to provide better returns than bank Fixed Deposits of similar duration.

etmCategoryList.name: HYBRID_ARBITRAGE
etmCategoryList.desc: Arbitrage funds are equity-oriented hybrid mutual funds that generate returns by using arbitrage meaning they exploit price differences of the same asset between cash and derivatives markets. They do this by buying in the cash market and selling in the futures market at the same time. Since the profit is largely locked in, returns tend to be relatively stable, making these funds suitable for investment horizons of 3 to 6 months, and even more efficient when held for over 1 year to benefit from equity taxation.

etmCategoryList.name: HYBRID_DYNAMIC_ASSET_ALLOCATION
etmCategoryList.desc: Balance Advantage Funds invest in a mix of stocks and FD-like instruments. However, they keep changing this allocation based on the market conditions to provide you optimal returns with minimal risk. Balance Advantage Funds also known as Dynamic Asset Allocation Funds.

etmCategoryList.name: HYBRID_MULTI_ASSET_ALLOCATION
etmCategoryList.desc: Multi Asset Allocation Funds are hybrid funds that must invest a minimum of 10% in at least 3 asset classes. These funds typically have a combination of equity, debt, and one more asset class like gold, real estate, etc.

etmCategoryList.name: EQUITY_FOCUSED
etmCategoryList.desc: Focused mutual funds are equity funds that follow a strategy of having a concentrated portfolio. These funds cannot have more than 30 stocks in their portfolio as per SEBI regulation, although there is no limitation on market cap or sectors it can invest.

etmCategoryList.name: THEMATIC-ESG
etmCategoryList.desc: Thematic-ESG funds are equity mutual funds that invest in companies aligned with a specific theme while also following environmental, social, and governance (ESG) principles. These funds are broader than sectoral funds, as they invest in companies and sectors united by a common idea.

etmCategoryList.name: EQUITY_FLEXI_CAP
etmCategoryList.desc: Flexi Cap funds invest in companies of all sizes and across sectors. This flexibility allows them to make changes in the portfolio as market conditions change.

etmCategoryList.name: DEBT_TARGET_MATURITY
etmCategoryList.desc: These funds aim to replicate an index of debt instruments. So, they invest in the underlying debt papers of an index in the exact same proportion. Fund manager does not actively buy and sell securities.

etmCategoryList.name: OTHERS_OTHERS
etmCategoryList.desc: These are unique ideas that fund houses come up with amid evolving investing and market trends.

etmCategoryList.name: EQUITY_DOMESTIC_FOF
etmCategoryList.desc: Invest in a fund that itself invests across multiple equity mutual funds — offering instant diversification across fund managers, market caps, and investment styles through a single investment.

etmCategoryList.name: EQUITY_RETIREMENT_SOLUTIONS
etmCategoryList.desc: These funds primarily invest in equities (at least 65% of their assets). They come with a lock-in of at least 5 years or till retirement, whichever is earlier.

etmCategoryList.name: EQUITY_CHILDREN_SOLUTIONS
etmCategoryList.desc: These funds primarily invest in equities (at least 65% of their assets). They come with a lock-in of at least 5 years or till the child turns major, whichever is earlier.

etmCategoryList.name: DEBT_RETIREMENT_SOLUTIONS
etmCategoryList.desc: These funds predominantly invest in debt instruments. They are suitable for either extremely conservative investors or those who are nearing retirement and don't want to risk their accumulated corpus.

etmCategoryList.name: HYBRID_RETIREMENT_SOLUTIONS
etmCategoryList.desc: These funds invest in a mix of equity and debt instruments. The asset mix helps lower the volatility than pure equity funds. You cannot redeem for at least 5 years or till retirement, whichever is earlier.

etmCategoryList.name: EQUITY_LARGE_CAP_INDEX
etmCategoryList.desc: These funds track different large-cap indices such as NIFTY 50, SENSEX, NIFTY Next 50, NIFTY 100, etc. These are low-cost index funds that track and mirror the underlying index.

etmCategoryList.name: EQUITY_MID_CAP_INDEX
etmCategoryList.desc: These funds do not try to outperform the index by actively selecting mid-cap stocks. Instead, they aim to replicate the performance of mid-cap indices like NIFTY Midcap 150 by holding the same stocks as the index in the same proportions.

etmCategoryList.name: EQUITY_SMALL_CAP_INDEX
etmCategoryList.desc: These funds aim to replicate the performance of small-cap indices like NIFTY Smallcap 250, BSE 250 Smallcap, etc. The idea is to invest in the same stocks as the index in the same proportions.

etmCategoryList.name: EQUITY_INTERNATIONAL_INDEX
etmCategoryList.desc: These equity funds aim to replicate the performance of a sector-specific index like banking, technology, infrastructure, etc.

etmCategoryList.name: DEBT_LONG_DEBT_INDEX
etmCategoryList.desc: These funds replicate an index comprising long-term debt papers. Typically, the securities are held till maturity and fund managers don't actively trade papers.

etmCategoryList.name: EQUITY_MULTICAP_INDEX
etmCategoryList.desc: These funds track indices that include large-cap, mid-cap and small-cap companies. So, the universe of stocks you invest in can be pretty broad.

etmCategoryList.name: EQUITY_LARGE_AND_MIDCAP_INDEX
etmCategoryList.desc: These funds track the top 250 companies by market cap. These include the top 100 large caps and the 150 mid-cap companies.

etmCategoryList.name: EQUITY-THEMATIC-QUANT-FUND
etmCategoryList.desc: These funds use quantitative tools to design algorithms. These algorithms help them pick stocks and also decide a stocks allocation in the fund.

etmCategoryList.name: HYBRID_TAX_EFFICIENT_INCOME
etmCategoryList.desc: Tax-efficient income funds are mutual funds that invest in units of debt-oriented schemes and arbitrage sche mes to generate stable returns with low risk.

etmCategoryList.name: Equity Opportunities
etmCategoryList.desc: Invest in funds that identify where we are in the economic cycle and rotate into sectors or companies best positioned to capitalise on emerging opportunities — dynamically shifting allocation as market conditions evolve.

etmCategoryList.name: THEMATIC-MANUFACTURING
etmCategoryList.desc: Invest in companies driving India's manufacturing growth — from industrial machinery and defence to chemicals and capital goods — poised to benefit from policy tailwinds and global supply chain shifts.

etmCategoryList.name: THEMATIC-INNOVATION
etmCategoryList.desc: Invest in companies at the forefront of disruptive technologies and breakthrough ideas — spanning AI, fintech, clean energy, and next-gen healthcare — that have the potential to reshape entire industries.
